purpose: Local replication of the Kaggle nightly-run failure and on-real-data verification of the fix in commit 10629e2 (exp2_league_fbhand CREATE hoisted above its consumers)

environment.method: chunked replication — synchronous short invocations, /tmp/mlb_cache parquet persisted across invocations via pull_statcast resume

ingestion.resume_path: Aug 1-31 fresh chunk, then Sep 1-30 forward top-up (cache merge + dedupe on pitch identity)

environment_degradations: il_stints_pitchers.parquet absent locally -> bullpen availability degrades to exposure 0 / count 0 (documented pre-availability semantics)
il_stints.parquet absent locally -> expected lineups fall back to participant pool, lineup_il_flag_* forced 0

exp2_source_coverage_pct.notes: 100% usage = COALESCE(usage, 0.0) known-zero fallback; 98.1% rates = league-rate fallback via ASOF join; the 15 missing rows per rate cell are exactly the Aug-1 day-1 slate (deliberate 0*NaN residual — no league history exists strictly prior to the first day); team-side gaps stay NaN by design

conclusion: The exact statement that raised duckdb.CatalogException ('Table with name exp2_league_fbhand does not exist!') at con.execute(_EXP2_SP_FBHAND_SQL) on the 2026-10-01 Kaggle run now executes successfully on real Statcast data, and every downstream consumer (exp2_sp_fbhand joins into game_level) produces populated columns. The fix works in production conditions.
scope_limits: Replication covered Phases 1-3 (ingestion + DuckDB feature build) — the phase that failed. Walk-forward/predict/push phases were NOT re-run locally (sandbox reaps long processes; walk already validated via the 20261001 exported-frame A/B gate and the 201-test battery at 10629e2).
Two-month window, not the full 2025-01-01..today production window (fold geometry and the ingestion min-games guard require the long window; the changed code path is window-independent).
